questions.stem: A fair six-sided dice is rolled 300 times. How many times would you expect to roll a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so P(>4) = 2/6 = 1/3. Expected outcomes = 300 × 1/3 = 100. A common error is including 4 (giving P = 3/6 = 1/2 and expected = 150).

questions.stem: A biased spinner has P(red) = 0.4, P(blue) = 0.35, P(green) = 0.25. In 400 spins, how many more times would you expect blue than green?
A bag contains 5 red and 15 blue balls. A ball is drawn, its colour noted, and returned. This is repeated 60 times. How many times would you expect to draw a red ball?
questions.explanation: P(red) = 5/20 = 1/4. Expected red draws = 60 × 1/4 = 15. Since balls are replaced, the probability stays the same each time.

questions.stem: A company expects 2% of its products to be defective. In a batch of 5000, how many defective items are expected?
questions.explanation: Expected defective = 5000 × 0.02 = 100. Option (a) calculates 5000 × 0.002. Option (d) calculates 5000 × 0.2 (using 20% instead of 2%).

questions.stem: Tom pays 50p to play a game. He rolls a dice: if he gets a 6 he wins £2, otherwise he wins nothing. He plays 120 times. What is his expected overall profit or loss?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 120 × £0.50 = £60. Expected wins = 120 × 1/6 = 20 wins at £2 each = £40. Overall = £40 − £60 = −£20 (a loss of £20).
